questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to plan a wedding
Why horse and carriage rides are rare
Why fewer people are marrying, and views on marriage
How divorce laws in the UK have changed over the last fifty years
questions.why: They discuss falling numbers of marriages and hear from two people with different views.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention a horse and carriage?
options: To say that, like carriages, marriage is becoming rarer
To suggest a way to travel to a wedding
To talk about old traditions in the countryside
To show that marriage is very old-fashioned
questions.why: He says carriages are rare now and 'marriage in the UK is getting rarer too'.

questions.q: What is the trend for opposite-sex marriages in the UK?
options: The numbers are rising
The numbers are staying the same
The numbers change a lot every year
The numbers are falling year on year
questions.why: Rob says 'the trend is downwards' with fewer couples marrying year on year.

questions.q: What does Tom think about marriage?
options: It is the best way to show love
It is old-fashioned, and he fears commitment
It is too expensive
It is good for society and makes relationships stronger
questions.why: Tom calls it 'a bit of an archaic concept' and says he's a commitment phobe.

questions.q: What does Tom say about his current relationship?
options: He is single
He is planning to get married
He is very happy in it
It has just ended
questions.why: Tom says 'although I am in a very happy relationship at the moment'.

questions.q: What is Dan's view of marriage?
options: It makes society more stable
It is only for religious people
It is not necessary any more
It makes people less free
questions.why: Dan says 'It has a very stabilising effect on society'.

questions.q: According to Dan, what else does marriage do?
options: Saves couples money
Makes families bigger
Makes people happier and more successful at work
Tells everyone you have found the right person
questions.why: He says it 'declares publicly to the world that you have found the right person for you'.

questions.q: What possible reason for fewer marriages does Neil suggest?
options: Weddings are too expensive
Children of divorced parents may be less likely to marry
People are too busy working to find time to plan a wedding
There are fewer places to get married
questions.why: Neil says with more divorces, 'perhaps children of divorced parents are less likely to get married'.
